title: O'Shaquie Foster dominates Emanuel Navarrete to unify titles at 130 pounds - CBS Sports
description: Foster put on a masterful performance to claim two more titles on Saturday
body:
Foster put on a masterful performance to claim two more titles on Saturday
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:15 am ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Performances in battles between champions are rarely more impressive than that which O'Shaquie Foster turned in against Emanuel Navarrete on Saturday in San Antonio. Foster brought the WBC junior lightweight championship to the ring and left with Navarrete's IBF and WBO belts.Foster set the tone early, leading the dance and picking the right moments to engage while avoiding Navarrete's attempts to push the action with his pressure-based game. In the opening round, Foster was so effective that Navarrete landed no punches in the frame.While the belief entering the fight was that the fight would ultimately be a battle between Foster's technique and Navarrete's willingness to engage in an ugly fight to land power shots, Foster made it clear as the rounds ticked by that he had no concerns about Navarrete's power, nor was he afraid to stand and put power behind his own shots.When Navarrete was able to land, Foster was always ready with a response, outlanding Navarrete and doing so with power and grit. It was the kind of performance Foster has always seemed capable of, but rarely displayed, which was why four of his previous five bouts had ended in either a majority or split decision.
Knowing the fight had slipped from his grasp by the championship rounds, Navarrete tried to find a home run shot that could erase the scorecard deficit, and he seemed close to finding that shot when an uppercut rattled Foster late in Round 11.While it seemed the uppercut may have set up a dramatic charge for Navarrete in the final round, it was Foster who landed a bomb in an exchange, dropping Navarrete to the canvas. While Navarrete attempted to argue that the referee should not have called that moment a knockdown, Foster left no doubt moments later, when another huge right sent Navarrete down for the second time in the round.Navarrete beat the count and made it to the end of the round, and the fight, but Foster was crowned unified champion by scores of 115-111, 118-108, 118-108.
"I knew he was going to be strong and awkward." Foster said after the fight. "He's a great champion. I just had a little more in me tonight. ... I told y'all before, I felt like I was the better inside fighter and the better outside fighter and I proved that tonight."

title: Brewers' Aaron Ashby on verge of MLB history amid dominant postseason run - CBS Sports
description: The lefty reliever has been the star of the best bullpen in history and now his team is two wins from its first W
body:
The lefty reliever has been the star of the best bullpen in history and now his team is two wins from its first World Series title
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:10 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        MILWAUKEE -- The final outs of Game 2 of the World Series belonged to Brewers lefty Aaron Ashby, not closer Trevor Megill. Not that labels matter much with this team. Manager Pat Murphy pieces things together the way it works best for his ballclub instead of managing to stats. Megill, for example, had 30 saves in the regular season, but Chad Patrick and Abner Uribe had six apiece. Ashby had four. Ashby gets so many important outs that, paired with the Brewers' relentless comebacks, he also recorded 13 regular-season wins. How about that? A reliever with 13 wins! Here in the playoffs, he now has one win and three saves. He's also absorbing multiple innings when called upon and has become one of the biggest postseason bullpen weapons we've ever seen. That isn't hyperbole. After the five-out save in Game 2 of the World Series, a 5-4 Brewers win that gives them a 2-0 lead in the best-of-seven series, Ashby's playoff stats are ridiculous. The line: 15 ⅔ IP, 5 H, 0 R, 3 BB, 17 K. 

        
            
                The Rays are making too many mistakes to stand a chance against the relentless Brewers
                
                    Matt Snyder                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The most consecutive scoreless innings to start a postseason in MLB history?2016 Andrew Miller: 16 2026 Aaron Ashby: 15 ⅔1984 Andy Hawkins: 15 ⅓1981 Goose Gossage: 14 ⅓Sure, Ashby was coming off a very good regular season, but he wasn't this level of bullpen killer. He had a 3.12 ERA and 1.31 WHIP. This is something entirely new.Not only that, but he's had razor-thin margins with which to work. In Game 1 of the NLDS, Ashby came in to a tie game and got all four Padres batters he faced out. The Brewers won (shocking, I know). In Game 2, he entered with the Brewers down by a run and he held it right there. They won in walk-off fashion. In Game 4, he entered with a one-run lead and worked three hitless, scoreless innings, grabbing the win (starter Robert Gasser failed to complete five innings).Onto the NLCS. In Game 1 against the Dodgers, Ashby came in with a one-run lead and went two innings without allowing a run. In Game 2, you guessed it, he came in with a one-run lead. He got the final five outs for a save. Sure enough, in the clinching Game 4, Ashby entered yet again with a one-run lead. He got a three-inning save to win the National League pennant. 
Thus far in the World Series, he's recorded 10 outs without allowing a run while protecting a two-run lead in Game 1 and a one-run lead in Game 2. Not too bad for a fourth-round draft pick out of Crowder College, huh?"He does what it takes," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said after the Game 2 win on Saturday. "It's unconventional. Multiple innings in relief. It's Goose Gossage-like. I guess we had a guy like that here too, Rollie [Fingers]. Multiple-inning relief. Sometimes you make mistakes, sometimes you go with it."The Brewers are a well-rounded ballclub. They are good at pretty much everything. The only aspect in which they don't particularly statistically excel is home runs, but they hit timely ones and have done so throughout the playoffs. The top of the rotation features extremely talented young arms. The bullpen is both deep and outstanding. Ashby, though, has been separating himself all playoffs. 
Aaron Ashby has been one of the greatest postseason relief weapons in MLB history. Now his team is just two wins from the championship.

title: Barcelona vs. Real Madrid: Who has the edge in El Clasico? - CBS Sports
description: The two Spanish giants will meet on Sunday in Barcelona for one of the most anticipated matches of the season
body:
The two Spanish giants will meet on Sunday in Barcelona for one of the most anticipated matches of the season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:06 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        On Sunday, Barcelona will host Real Madrid at the Spotify Camp Nou for what's expected to be one of the most exciting moments of the season. On top of that, Sunday's game will feature the return of Jose Mourinho to the stadium where he fought some of his incredible battles against Barcelona from 2010 to 2013, when he coached Real Madrid for the first time. The reception is expected to be heated, especially considering what happened in the recent weeks. Real Madrid striker Vinicius Jr. will miss El Clasico against FC Barcelona after being suspended for four games for the red card he received in Real Madrid's home game against Villarreal at the Bernabeu last week. Despite the appeal, Vinicius Jr. won't be part of the game and will be back playing for the Blancos after the international break in the domestic league. Let's take a closer look at both squads and compare their strengths to determine which team has the edge: GoalkeepersLet's start with the goalkeepers, and here Thibaut Courtois is probably still one of the best in his role and can directly make an impact on the result of a match. Joan Garcia, on the other hand, still has some room for improvement, and he's at a different stage of his career, with plenty of potential to evolve more. Although Courtois is nine years older than Garcia, making a direct comparison is somewhat unfair given their different stages of development; the Real Madrid goalkeeper still has the edge right now in terms of experience, consistency, and overall quality. At least when he's fit. 
Barcelona: Joan Garcia, Wojciech Szczęsny, Dominik Livakovic.Real Madrid: Thibaut Courtois, Andriy Lunin, Fran Gonzalez. Edge: Real MadridDefenseThings get more complicated when it comes to the defensive lines. Both Barcelona and Real Madrid have strong lineups in these roles, but they also concede a lot of goals. The new Real Madrid signings such as Denzel Dumfries, Marc Cucurella or Ibrahima Konate are yet to show their full potential, while the Barcelona young defenders like Pau Cubarsi, Eric Garcia or Xavi Espart are showing to be in a better form. Barcelona: Joao Cancelo, Alejandro Balde, Pau Cubarsi, Xavi Espart, Andreas Christensen, Gerard Martin, Jules Kounde, Eric Garcia.Real Madrid: Raul Asencio, Eder Militao, Dean Huijsen, Trent Alexander-Arnold, Ibrahima Konate, Marc Cucurella, Alvaro Carreras, Antonio Rüdiger, Ferland Mendy, Denzel Dumfries.
Edge: BarcelonaMidfieldBoth sides have some incredibly talented players, as usual. Barcelona signed Rodri in the summer, after the Spanish captain refused to join Real Madrid before signing for the Blaugrana. Apart from that, the players in the roster led by Jose Mourinho are just as incredible: Jude Bellingham, Federico Valverde, Arda Guler, Aurelien Tchouameni and Bernardo Silva, who signed as a free agent in the summer. Despite the qualities of the Barcelona midfielders, Real Madrid look much stronger in this sector. Barcelona: Brian Farinas, Gavi, Fermin Lopez, Pedri, Rodri, Dani Olmo, Frenkie de Jong, Marc Bernal.Real Madrid: Jude Bellingham, Eduardo Camavinga, Federico Valverde, Aurelien Tchouameni, Arda Guler, Bernardo Silva, Thiago Pitarch, Jorge Cestero.
Edge: Real MadridForwards The most challenging one. It's almost impossible to decided between Lamine Yamal, Kylian Mbappe, Yan Diomande, Raphinha, Anthony Gordon and more. But there is a big difference ahead of Sunday's game: the absence of Vinicius Jr., who will miss El Clasico after receiving a four-game ban. Even if he didn't have his best start to the season so far, there is a difference without him. This is why I'm going for Barcelona this time. Barcelona: Gabriel Jesus, Lamine Yamal, Raphinha, Karim Adeyemi, Anthony Gordon, Roony Bardghji, Jesse Bisiwu, Hamza Abdelkarim.Real Madrid: Vinicius Junior, Endrick, Kylian Mbappe, Rodrygo, Cristian Espi, Brahim Díaz, Yan Diomande.
Edge: BarcelonaCoachThis is arguably one of the most difficult calls to make as both managers are considered among the best around the world. While Jose Mourinho shaped the last two decades of the game, Hansi Flick is now doing it as well. With two LaLiga titles won in his first two years at Barcelona, Flick now needs to win outside the country as he did at Bayern Munich before. Mourinho was called back by Real Madrid owner Florentino Perez to re-establish Real Madrid supremacy in Spain, but it won't be easy at all against Flick and Barcelona. Barcelona: Hansi FlickReal Madrid: Jose MourinhoEdge: Barcelona

title: Tomorrow's Top 25 Today projects college football rankings after Week 8 - CBS Sports
description: Another week in the 2026 season has brought about another round of upsets, and after multiple losses to top-10 teams, there are set to b
body:
Another week in the 2026 season has brought about another round of upsets, and after multiple losses to top-10 teams, there are set to be some more changes to the new college football rankings. No. 2 BYU and No. 8 Texas Tech each took their first loss of the season to unranked opponents, while No. 7 Ole Miss lost at No. 19 Texas and No. 8 Utah survived an upset scare from No. 14 Houston. If you combine those results with No. 15 Iowa and No. 16 USC both taking their second losses of the season, both to unranked teams, we have a week where the very top of the rankings might be easier to figure out than most of the spots outside the top 10. No. 1 Miami made things easy by putting a 50-burger on the board against Pitt, and more than half of the top five were off in Week 8 to provide very little room for upward momentum. But some of the changes further down in the rankings, including the result of Texas' win against Ole Miss, present the voters with unique challenges. How should voters react, for example, to the fact that Texas has a trio of great wins but also two stunning losses? The Longhorns were projected to be one of the best teams in the country, and they have provided results that make them merely one of the "very good" teams as October comes to a close. The good news for Texas, from a rankings perspective, is that "very good" seems to be good enough to sneak back into the top 10, which is an ideal spot for a College Football Playoff hopeful.  
Another thing to watch is a much more dispersed set of ballots. Last week the voters were extremely dialed in on the top 25. Most voters saw eye-to-eye on the top 24 teams in the country, and then everyone seemed to have their own unique flavor for No. 25. Last week only 32 teams received votes in the balloting, and this week it would not be a surprise at all to see as many as 40 teams getting a look for those last two or three spots on the ballot after multiple ranked losses outside the top 10.Here's how we think the new AP Top 25 will look on Sunday after Week 8. 1. Miami (Last week -- 1): The Hurricanes played their first game as the No. 1 team in the country since 2002 and quickly made it clear there would not be a third straight week of change at the top of the poll. Miami raced out to a 17-0 lead and went to the locker room up 31-7, tacking on a couple extra scores after halftime to cruise to a 52-23 win. A win as AP No. 1 is yet another marker of success for Mario Cristobal, who got to honor the 2001 title team with some throwback uniforms and a final score fitting of their title standard.   2. Ohio State (3): The Buckeyes were off in Week 8 and will be back in action next week at USC. 
3. Notre Dame (4): The Fighting Irish were off in Week 8 and will be back in action next week against Navy at home. 4. Georgia (5): The Bulldogs were off in Week 8 and will be back in action next week in their annual rivalry game against Florida. 5. BYU (2): Our projection here is that the voters will not, in the consensus, be respecting the head-to-head result of BYU over Notre Dame in their reassessment of the Cougars. Even though that game happened just one week ago, voters tend to be harsher with their reactions when top teams lose to unranked opponents. Still, the Notre Dame win on its own stands as better than anything some of the other one-loss teams have inside the top-10. That sets up a pretty high floor for any sensible readjustment to BYU's spot on the ballot. 
6. Indiana (6): Some voters may shift their ballots based on the Hoosiers' gritty-but-ugly win in overtime against Michigan. It was one of the biggest games of the day and featured zero touchdowns in regulation. The aesthetics of the result are likely to lead to some shifting of opinion among the AP voters. 7. UCLA (9): A slow start created some uneasiness around UCLA's big-time spotlight on CBS, but the Bruins played a much more effective second half and improved to 7-0 on the season with a 28-10 win against Michigan State. Two first-half fumbles kept the game close, but Michigan State's offense never posed much of a threat against a Bruins defense that has become a driving factor of their success over the last four games. 8. Utah (10): The Utes showed off their electric and tough home environment in a wild finish against No. 14 Houston, holding on to win 21-13 after snatching the game away in the fourth quarter. The game was 3-0 at halftime and an absolute grind with Utah getting no points out of a couple early drives due to an interception and a late missed field goal. But in the second half things started clicking a little bit more and Utah's defense stepped up big with a fumble recovery and a fourth down stop in the fourth quarter. It's a great win for a team that needed some validation to its rankings profile, and will have the Utes moving up inside the top 10.  
9. Kentucky (12): On a very busy night across college football, Kentucky did the best thing a ranked team could do and stayed quiet. The Wildcats got a good push from Vanderbilt early but reclaimed command of the game and poured it on late for a 34-17 win against the Commodores. Will Stein's team is now 7-1 overall and 5-1 in the SEC, standing firm as a realistic contender for a top-10 ranking at the end of the season.  10. Texas (19): The Longhorns snapped their two-game skid with a thunderous top-10 win against Ole Miss, setting up the most complicated profile of the week for AP voters. Texas has wins against Ohio State, Ole Miss and Tennessee, yet also two losses on its profile. As it washes out for voters, we expect Texas will be right in the mix as the top two-loss team in the country, which puts it in the range of jumping back into the top 10.11. Alabama (13): Tuscaloosa was another spot where it looked like we could see another upset, but the Crimson Tide flipped the game on Texas A&M with a 14-0 fourth quarter to pull away from an 11-point win. Keelon Russell got back on track with 311 passing yards and three touchdowns, sending Alabama into the off week with a 6-2 record.    
12. Texas Tech (8): The strength of Texas Tech's placement in the rankings was its unbeaten status, and after Saturday's loss at Cincinnati, the Red Raiders' resume is going to face much tougher scrutiny. The good news is that the team has an early-season quality win to bolster its profile, having defeated Houston back in September.  13. Wake Forest (17): The Demon Deacons were off in Week 8 and will be back in action next week against Virginia. 14. Ole Miss (7): The head-to-head advantage against LSU serves as a nice landing spot for voters looking to move Ole Miss down after the loss at Texas. The Rebels did not play a particularly clean game but also were not outclassed in any way that would dramatically change the way they are viewed against their peers. Ole Miss has two wins against ranked opponents (LSU, Missouri) and two losses against ranked opponents (Texas, Florida) to make them the perfect middle-of-the-pack teams in a midseason AP Top 25 poll. 
15. LSU (18): The off week arrives with Lane Kiffin's Tigers sitting at 6-2 overall but still lacking the high-end wins that can make an argument for big moves up in the rankings. LSU's ceiling is clearly higher than its current ranking, and those opportunities will come on the other side of the bye with Alabama, Texas and Tennessee in consecutive weeks.  16. Florida (20): The Gators were off in Week 8 and will be back in action next week against Georgia. 17. Tennessee (11): Beating Alabama had the Vols firing up the rankings past a Texas team that it had lost to earlier in the season. Now at 6-2 after losing to South Carolina on a walk-off field goal, voters are going to group Tennessee in with a cluster of quality two-loss teams in the SEC. Unlike BYU, there might not be as much of a hit for the "loss to an unranked team" adjustment here, since oddsmakers did have South Carolina as the narrow favorite heading into the game.   
18. Boise State (21): Add the Broncos as another team that got off to a bit of a slow start in a tricky spot before righting the ship late. Boise State was tied 10-10 at Washington State late in the third quarter but scored three fourth-quarter touchdowns to pull away for a 31-10 win that looks much better to voters scanning the top 25 scoreboard.  19. Missouri (22): The Tigers were off in Week 8 and will be back in action next Saturday night against Arkansas. 20. SMU (23): Kevin Jennings passed Tanner Mordecai for the SMU career passing touchdowns record with three scores through the air, and running back Kendrick Raphael scored three times (two rushing, one receiving) against his former team in a 59-20 win against Cal. 
21. Northwestern (24): We are not projecting voters to overreact in the wake of beating Rutgers, but the Wildcats continue to prove their worth as one of the best teams in the Big Ten. Northwestern is now 6-1 overall, with the lone loss coming to Indiana by six points. There's admittedly not a lot of meat to the profile in terms of high-end wins, but the way this offense can get downhill when it's rolling is impressive. Aidan Chiles was the star on Saturday in the 42-14 win against the Scarlet Knights, totaling five touchdowns (three passing, two rushing) in the victory.  22. Arizona (25): On a day that saw close to maximum carnage in the Big 12, it was Arizona that stayed steady. The Wildcats never gave Iowa State an inch of breathing room and rode their defense to a comfortable win, improving to 6-1 on the season.23. Houston (14): The Cougars are set for a drop to the edge of the top 25 after giving up the lead late at Utah. Houston struggled to get control early when it was getting stops and now sit at 6-2 with last week's close win against Oklahoma State serving as a landing spot in the rankings.      
24. Oklahoma State (NR): If just nine of the 41 voters who did not have Oklahoma State on last week's ballot had put them at No. 25, then the Cowboys probably don't fall out of the rankings after a loss to Houston. As it is, they finished 26th in the voting points and are now set up for an easy bump back into the rankings after a 57-24 win against Colorado. While the Oregon win does not have the pop it once did, the Pokes did beat a Ducks team that had Dante Moore and also took care of business against the same UCF team that just beat BYU. 25. Wisconsin (NR): One read of Wisconsin's profile from a rankings perspective might be the "quality loss" boost, considering the Badgers are now 5-2 with the only losses coming to Notre Dame and UCLA. But Wisconsin didn't just beat USC on Saturday night in Madison; it put the clamps on an offense that we know has enough talent to overwhelm lesser competition. In the wake of the 24-7 win against the Trojans, we're projecting a move up into the top 25 that would mark the program's first AP poll appearance since 2023, Luke Fickell's second season in Madison. Projected to drop out: No. 15 Iowa, No. 16 USC

title: 2026 WNBA Finals: Game 6 location up in the air for Dream vs. Valkyries - CBS Sports
description: The Atlanta Hawks are scheduled to play at State Farm Arena on Thursday night, which leaves the Dream scrambling
body:
The Atlanta Hawks are scheduled to play at State Farm Arena on Thursday night, which leaves the Dream scrambling for an alternative
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:20 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Golden State Valkyries held off the Atlanta Dream's comeback attempt on Saturday to secure a 67-62 win in Game 4 of the 2026 WNBA Finals. The result evened the series at 2-2 and ensured that the series will return to Atlanta for Game 6 -- though where, specifically, remains to be seen. The location for Game 6 on Thursday is still officially listed as "TBD" on the schedule due to a conflict with State Farm Arena. The Atlanta Hawks, State Farm Arena's primary tenant, are scheduled to host the Cleveland Cavaliers that night. Tip-off for the Hawks game is set for 7 p.m. ET, while tip-off for Game 6 is set for 8 p.m. ET. Obviously, State Farm Arena cannot host two games at the same time, which means one, or both, of the games will have to be adjusted. The WNBA did not have an update to share when reached for comment by CBS Sports. The Dream's primary home is Gateway Center Arena in College Park, which is the league's smallest venue and has a capacity of just 3,500. That is not an ideal setting for a Finals game -- or any playoff game -- and the Dream have played all five of their postseason contests at State Farm Arena. That included Games 3 and 4 of the Finals, which had to be moved due to other conflicts. Game 3 was moved from Oct. 22 to Oct. 21 to avoid a Sombr concert, while Game 4 was moved up to 1 p.m. ET to accommodate the Hawks' home opener against the Houston Rockets on Saturday; the NBA game was shifted back to 8:30 p.m. ET. 
There is less flexibility for both parties moving forward, however, so it's unclear what will happen with Game 6. Here are a few options:Move Game 6 to Wednesday: This is not possible because the Hawks are also at home that night against the Miami Heat.Move Game 6 to Friday: That is not possible because it would create a back-to-back with Game 7, which is set for Saturday in San Francisco, if necessary.Move the Hawks' game: The Hawks also play on Wednesday, but are off on Friday before playing again on Saturday. The Cavaliers, the Hawks' opponent on Thursday, are also off Friday before playing again on Saturday. State Farm Arena has an open date for Friday, so it would be possible to move the Hawks-Cavaliers game to Friday, but that would require multiple NBA franchises, the NBA and broadcast partners to sign off. Play a doubleheader: The Dream and Hawks played a doubleheader at State Farm on Saturday. Could they do it again on Thursday? No. Again, the Hawks play on Wednesday night, so they could not turn around and play on Thursday afternoon. And there's no way WNBA would host Game 6 of the Finals, which will be a potential clincher for one of the two teams, on a Thursday afternoon. Play Game 6 at Gateway Center: This is the easiest solution. It would not be ideal to host Game 6 of the Finals at a 3,500-seat venue, but Gateway Center is the Dream's primary home and there would be no logistical challenges. Play Game 6 at another arena in Atlanta: The Dream could try to move Game 6 to another venue in Atlanta. But where? Gas South Arena holds 13,000, but has a concert scheduled for Thursday. McCamish Pavilion on Georgia Tech's campus -- where the Dream played for two seasons from 2017-18 -- holds 8,600 and has an open date on Thursday. The Georgia State Convocation Center holds 7,500 and appears to have an open date on Thursday as well. Those would be the two best options if the WNBA and the Dream want a bigger crowd, but the Dream haven't played at either venue this season. Would they want to play the biggest game of their season at an unfamiliar venue? After Game 4, Angel Reese made it clear that she hopes the WNBA can find a way to get Game 6 at State Farm Arena. Here's her exchange with a reporter during the postgame press conference:
Question: It took quite a bit to get these Games 3 and 4 moved here, and now that you know you will need a Game 6, what's your hope or expectation of what that would look like coming back to Atlanta?Reese: Just them showing up again. The fan support here has been amazing. We appreciate the love and support and everybody coming out. And being able to force a Game 6 at least. Being able to come here and play in front of the home crowd again would be amazing.Question: Here or Gateway?Reese: HereEarlier this month, the Dream announced a multi-year deal to play all home games at State Farm Arena, starting with the 2027 season, thereby avoiding any such conflicts in the future. Unfortunately for them, that doesn't solve the Game 6 dilemma.

body:
The Dream and Valkyries are battling in the 2026 WNBA Finals, with the series now knotted at 2
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:50 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Adam Eargle, CBS Sports
            
            

    
        The WNBA Finals are knotted at two apiece after the Golden State Valkyries held on for a Game 4 win on Sunday over the Atlanta Dream. Defense stole the show for Golden State, aided by a poor showing from Dream star Angel Reese, in a 67-62 final score.The series resumes on Monday in San Francisco as the Valkyries host Game 5. Both teams are looking to win a title for the first time in franchise history.The Dream and Valkyries both completed semifinal sweeps, giving them a week off before the Finals. Atlanta knocked out the New York Liberty, while Golden State ousted the reigning champion Las Vegas Aces. The Dream knocked the Washington Mystics out in the first round and are a perfect 5-0 in the playoffs. The Valkyries defeated the Dallas Wings in the first round, needing all three games to do so. The Finals, for the second season ever, are a best-of-seven series in 2026.The 2026 WNBA season has been groundbreaking, on and off the court. It launched on the heels of a contentious and extended labor battle that resulted in a historic raise for the players (the salary cap increased from $1.5 million in 2025 to $7 million in 2026), and in return, the players raised the bar on a weekly basis.         New York Giants coach John Harbaugh saw more than enough from J.J. McCarthy during the fourth quarter of last week's loss to give him the starting nod in Sunday's matchup with the Houston Texans.After coming off the bench to replace Jameis Winston and lead three scoring drives in the final 10 minutes, the leash is coming off McCarthy for a team in dire need of consistent quarterback play with Jaxson Dart on the shelf for the rest of the campaign.With New York's bye week on the way after Sunday's game, it would be quite a surge of momentum to beat the Texans. The Giants would also pick up some confidence before the start of November, potentially 4-2-1 and atop the NFC East."What gives us the best chance to be our best? Gives us the best chance to play the best offense we can, and I thought Jameis has done a tremendous job," Harbaugh said this week on his decision. "Won us games, played well. But as we go forward here, this is going to be our direction, and we think it gives us some good options on offense."
Harbaugh said the move to McCarthy after a month is due in part to giving the franchise's freshest quarterback time in a different system following a trade with the Minnesota Vikings. Harbaugh joked that not even Tom Brady would be able to start immediately for a new team if he came out of retirement ready to go, given the complexities of learning a different playbook.Winston threw for 957 yards, seven touchdowns and five interceptions in five games after the injury to Dart, going 2-2-1 overall."Both guys are great quarterbacks. It's not really a comparison kind of thing," Harbaugh said. "Just, you know, J.J.'s got a skill set that we can take advantage of, and we're excited to see what we can do with it. He's obviously out here throwing right now. I'm kind of watching him as you guys ask the questions out here, getting some extra work. 
"He's got a heck of a skill set, you know? He can throw it. He's picked up the offense really quickly. He's an athletic guy, obviously, and he's going to play some good football."Offensive coordinator Matt Nagy and quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan have spent the last few weeks with McCarthy, assuring Harbaugh that the third-year pro is ready to operate at full efficiency."The offense is — the book itself is huge, and it's always tailored toward probably your players, and certainly your quarterback, right? But he's got the game plan down," Harbaugh said. "I think he headed down last week, pretty fully, even more so this week. It has been tailored a little more toward his direction, probably, but he'll be ready to go."
McCarthy, a former first-round pick, told reporters this week he was "honored" to be named New York's Week 7 QB1."You know, thrilled to get out there, and tomorrow really get in the film room and just evaluate today's practice and get better, and go from there," McCarthy said.

        One week after upsetting Notre Dame, No. 2 BYU lost a road thriller 39-31 against UCF in double-overtime. The Knights stopped the Cougars on fourth down to stun BYU and beat their first AP Top 5 team in program history. UCF initially had to settle for a field goal in double-overtime, but a questionable roughing the kicker call turned three points into a first-and-goal from the four-yard line. Quarterback Keyone Jenkins found Utah native Gabe Brousseau four a touchdown and Tyren Hornes on the two-point conversion. BYU went to the air as quarterback Bear Bachmeier was just short on a touchdown to wide receiver Kyle Kasper. They reached second-and-goal from the four-yard line, but Bachmeier threw three incompletions on tough passes to end the game as fans stormed the field. Jenkins, the backup quarterback at UCF, threw for 293 yards, rushed for 35 and scored four touchdowns in a masterful effort. BYU got three touchdowns from quarterback Bear Bachmeier, but UCF's defense stood up at the biggest moment. 
This was the first loss for BYU against an unranked opponent since a 17-13 loss to Kansas on Nov. 16, 2024. Wild end of regulationWith seconds remaining in regulation, BYU appeared to force a strip-sack to reach overtime. The Knights were on the edge of field goal range and would have had a chance to win. Replay review revealed that Knights quarterback Keyone Jenkins was pushing his arm forward with control. title: UFC 333 results, takeaways: Alexander Volkanovski reminds of his greatness - CBS Sports
description: Volkanovski and Yan showed why they might be all-time greats in their respective weight classes on Saturday
body:
Volkanovski and Yan showed why they might be all-time greats in their respective weight classes on Saturday
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:51 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Following a thrilling fight card and two spectacular title defenses at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi, there is certainly plenty to talk about. Alexander Volkanovski, at 38, passed Brazilian legend Jose Aldo for the most title wins in featherweight history by stopping unbeaten Movsar Evloev in the main event. In the five-round thriller of a co-feature, Petr Yan defended his 135-pound title with a come-from-behind decision win over Merab Dvalishvili in the third meeting between bantamweight legends. Let's take a closer look at the biggest takeaways from what took place inside Etihad Arena. 1. Alexander Volkanovski called his shot and absolutely deliveredAdmittedly, I really didn't know what to make of the 38-year-old living legend's prediction earlier this week when he said that the unbeaten Evloev was a problem for the rest of the division but just not for him and that he would score an early stoppage. Some passed off those words as gamesmanship with Volkanovski hoping to get Evloev off his game or discourage him from wrestling. Not only was the two-time featherweight king true to his words in finishing Evloev inside of two rounds with pinpoint striking, he neutralized just about every aspect of his younger opponent's game in the process. Craig Jones, who was in Volkanovski's corner as a grappling coach, also suggested on social media after the fight that the champion was battling the flu during fight week. Volkanovski, who also equaled Aldo's UFC record for featherweight title defenses (along with owning a 2019 win over him), didn't just cement himself as the greatest 145-pound fighter of all time, he continued to redefine what longevity looks like in the lower weight classes. It's not hyperbole to say that Volkanovski is one of the 10 best fighters in the sport's history. And he's not done yet. 
2. Petr Yan did what likely no other bantamweight could have doneFrom the broken hand Yan entered with in their first meeting in 2023 to the fact that Dvalishivili took their rematch in December on just a two-month turnaround as he ambitiously looked to set the record for title defenses in a calendar year, both fighters entered Saturday's trilogy with legitimate excuses for their defeats. But 10 months after their rematch, with Yan recently healed from back surgery, the third meeting between these legends was a fast-paced and very technical thriller as a rejuvenated Dvalishvili dominated the opening two rounds with his spamming wrestling attack until Yan made the midfight adjustments and used his striking to hurt the former champion down the stretch in a comeback win. Three years after Dvalishvili set a new UFC record for takedown attempts with 49 in their first meeting, he upped that record to an absolutely insane 58 in their trilogy. Every single other bantamweight in the world would've eventually succumbed to Dvalishvili's pressure on this night. He was that dialed in and showcased a variety of new entry points and angles for his takedown attempts. But for the second straight fight, Yan completely took away the superhuman part of Dvalishvili's game that the rest of the division -- throughout the former champion's incredible 14-fight win streak -- were routinely humbled by. Yan's combination of stamina, IQ, toughness and striking technique was legendary on this night as many began to call him, quite possibly, the best bantamweight fighter in history. But it's all part of a larger career comeback story that still isn't getting the attention it deserves as one of the more feel-good developments the sport has produced of late. Yan had both of his young sons by his side on this evening as he entered true living legend status in the sport's history. 
3. Despite solid win, Alexander Volkov likely still in wait-and-see modeFor all of the talk about how much the native of Russia has already done enough to earn a heavyweight title shot yet keeps getting passed over, it's hard not to avoid the feeling that his hard-fought victory over Rizvan Kuniev on Saturday -- on Volkov's 38th birthday -- still might not be enough. To Volkov's credit, he used his post-fight interview to challenge UFC CEO and president Dana White with the same shtick he brought to his surprise cameo at the final press conference just days earlier. Against Kuniev, Volkov did what he always does. He controlled distance, landed the better strikes and avoided allowing his opponent to take over the terms of the fight. And now, with seven wins in his last eight fights (and the only loss being a highly disputed decision in his 2024 rematch with current champion Ciryl Gane), Volkov remains in a great spot within the title hunt. Yet, sadly, he still doesn't feel like a slam dunk choice for the winner of the Gane's first title defense against Josh Hokit next month. Not with superstar Alex Pereira looking to rebound from his loss to Gane at the White House in June by fighting Sergei Pavlovich in December. Credit to Volkov for moving the chains and letting his voice be heard, but his fate still resides in the hands of UFC matchmakers. 4. No need to worry: Lone'er Kavanagh still looks like the future at flyweightFor a 125-pound division that has become the darling of the sport over the past year thanks to the breakout success of 24-year-old champion Joshua Van, it was good to see such a hyped prospect as Kavanagh rebound from a recent stretch of two stoppage defeats in three fights. The 27-year-old native of London was just three months removed from a submission loss to veteran contender Brandon Royval, which heavily muted the momentum he had built to open 2026 when Kavanagh took a short-notice fight at altitude in Mexico City and defeated two-time champion Brandon Moreno. Kavanagh entered quite a stern test in the form of a streaking Ramazan Temirov, the Uzbekistan native who had won his last 12 including all three walks to the Octagon. Kavanagh effectively tamed the aggressive knockout puncher in Temirov and relied upon his speed, defense and technique to expose the more raw and wild parts of his opponent's offensive game. Yet, it was a brutal pair of uppercuts that were most impressive as Kavanagh needed less than one round to make a statement thanks to his fast combination striking that he's still a very serious threat to the flyweight title. 
5. Abdul Rakhman Yakhyaev looks ready (right now) for the top light heavyweightsAt just 25, the native of Russia fits his nickname of "The Hunter" well with an 11-0 career record and 10 finishes. Normally, there wouldn't be much of a need to put the rocket ship on such a young fighter who is 4-0 since making his UFC debut last November. But the combination of the division's glaring lack of depth and the fact that Yakhyaev looks like a finished product already brings the need for an exception. Yakhyaev stepped up considerably in class on Saturday against Nikita Krylov and despite suffering a bloody nose in the early going, he absolutely dominated the battle-tested veteran in all aspects en route to a first-round TKO. Yakhyaev, who recorded the finish with a brutal knee to the head along the cage, called for a top-five opponent next during his post-fight interview. Let's cut to the chase: Yakhyaev is ready.

title: UFC 333 results: Petr Yan bests Merab Dvalishvili in trilogy bout to retain title - CBS Sports
description: Yan started slow but picked up the pace quickly to take control of the action over 25 minutes
body:
Yan started slow but picked up the pace quickly to take control of the action over 25 minutes
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:44 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Petr Yan had to dig deep in his bantamweight championship defense against Merab Dvalishvili at UFC 333, but he was able to put on one of the most impressive performances of his career to win a rubber match over the former champion.Dvalishvili won their first meeting in 2023 before going on to claim the title Yan had previously held. Yan kicked off his second reign as champion this past December, avenging that loss with a decision win over Dvalishvili.Be sure to keep up with all the action on Saturday with our live coverage of UFC 333, including round-by-round scoring and updated fight results throughout the night!Dvalishvili, being a notably faster starter than Yan, brought an expected high-energy approach to the start of the fight. Dvalishvili came out firing big right hands and pushing for takedowns, though Yan capably fended off the takedown attempts to keep the fight standing, and quickly got to his feet in the moments when Dvalishvili was able to finish a takedown attempt. Despite Yan's strong grappling defense, Dvalishvili's constant movement and attack put Yan in a position where he was unable to use his own offensive tools.
Yan landed some hard punches in the early stages of the second round, but Dvalishvili's pace continued to dictate the action, and he was able to get inside and work for takedowns, putting constant pressure on Yan, even when Yan was able to fend off the takedown attempts. Yan's moments were coming in spurts while Dvalishvili was keeping the faucet all the way open.
While things looked as though they'd continue to play out as they had been early in the third round, Yan went back to a tool that had worked well in the rematch, a hard left kick to the body that sent Dvalishvili stumbling backward grabbing at his liver. Dvalishvili recovered, but Yan finished the third having suddenly found success with repeated striking combinations.Yan continued to build on that momentum in Round 4, bringing a constant stream of slick boxing to land to Dvalishvili's head and body. The shots to the body especially seemed to bother Dvalishvili, and Yan was also consistent in fending off Dvalishvili's increasingly desperate takedown attempts.
Despite Dvalishvili's legendary motor and cardio, Yan appeared to be the fresher fighter in the final round, and he used that energy to continue putting big strikes on Dvalishvili.The question at the end of five rounds was who took the third round on the official scorecards. Dvailishvili clearly won the first half of the fight, and the third round, but was Yan's big momentum-turning moment with the body kick in Round 3 enough to retain the title? From that kick onward, the fight had been entirely Yan's.When the official scorecards were read, all three judges saw the fight 48-47 for Yan, winning him the rivalry with an incredible performance where he outlasted and outthought Dvalishvili.
Speaking through an interpreter after the fight, Yan made it clear he knew he could not afford to take his foot off the gas when the fight was entering it's final stages."I was listening to my coach," Yan said. "And he said, 'Look, we're going to the fifth round, and it's two-two. You win the round, you win the fight.'"

description: BYU and Texas Tech dealt a massive blow to the Big 12's playoff hopes, the Hurricanes rolled behind a dominant of
body:
BYU and Texas Tech dealt a massive blow to the Big 12's playoff hopes, the Hurricanes rolled behind a dominant offense and Dave Aranda's Baylor tenure reached a breaking point
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:55 am ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The chaotic college football season rolls on as Week 8 delivered even more upsets. No. 2 BYU, No. 7 Ole Miss, No. 8 Texas Tech and No. 15 Iowa all fell in stunning upsets, while No. 6 Indiana and No. 13 Alabama survived scares. Heading into the night slate, No. 1 Miami, No. 9 UCLA and No. 10 Utah are the only undefeated teams remaining. The last time three or fewer undefeated major college football teams remained through Oct. 24 was 1977, when Texas, Louisiana Tech and Colgate (!) all remained spotless. It's also the first time since 2007 that an AP Top-2 team lost against an unranked opponent in three straight weeks. The losses have completely shaken up the College Football Playoff and conference championship races, especially in the Big 12. Suddenly, the bottom half of the field is wide open and will be determined on the field. Here are the biggest winners and losers of Week 8 heading into primetime. Loser: The Big 12All week, the conversation has focused on the once-in-a-lifetime opportunity facing the Big 12. Had the league powers taken care of business, the league would have had a realistic shot at three College Football Playoff teams. After a chaotic Week 8, that path is diminished. 
No. 2 BYU struggled to maintain its momentum after stunning Notre Dame a week ago, losing a 39-31 decision against UCF in double overtime. No. 8 Texas Tech's struggles also caught up to it as the Red Raiders fell 37-24 against Cincinnati. When the rankings come out on Sunday, there will likely be only two Big 12 teams in the top 12 and none in the AP top five. It took one week for the league to waste its early lead. Winner: MiamiAs many of the top teams in America struggle, Miami is taking full advantage. The Hurricanes have a manageable schedule in the ACC, but they continue to obliterate overmatched opponents. 
This week, they dominated Pittsburgh 52-23 to reach 7-0 and 5-0 in ACC play. Hurricanes quarterback Darian Mensah threw for 387 yards and four touchdowns, but wide receiver Malachi Toney was more impressive with 194 yards and three touchdowns on 16 catches. Miami earned its first AP No. 1 ranking since 2002 this week. They look the part. 
        
            
                'The U' is back at No. 1, but Miami's quest for a legacy worthy of nostalgia is just beginning
                
                    Chip Patterson                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Loser: USCThe Trojans entered the season with high expectations, but a 24-7 loss to Wisconsin officially derails the hype train. USC rushed for a cool -17 yards as two early interceptions set the tone. Wisconsin only had to drive the length of the field one time for a touchdown, but that was still enough to put the Trojans to sleep. 
The seven-point performance marks the worst showing of Lincoln Riley's career, surpassing a 27-14 loss to Baylor in 2021 while at Oklahoma. Wisconsin has certainly improved, but the Trojans haven't looked the part of even a top 25 team. Winner: Texas running gameIt took yet another bad interception from Texas quarterback Arch Manning, but Steve Sarkisian finally trusted his running game down the stretch. Raleek Brown bullied his way all the way down the field to set up a 1-yard touchdown run from Manning. Then, Brown set up a game-sealing field goal with a 28-yard rush on second-and-10. Brown finished with 157 yards on 23 carries as part of a 200-yard rushing day for the Texas running backs without Hollywood Smothers available. The Rebels have some deficiencies against the run, but hopefully Sarkisian takes this as a lesson: Run the ball! 
Loser: Baylor coach Dave ArandaLosing to rival TCU last week was a bad sign, but falling 25-24 to Kansas is the final nail in the coffin for Aranda's tenure. For all the faults of the Aranda era, Baylor had a 14-game winning streak against the Jayhawks dating back to the 2007 season. Even during miserable 2-7 and 1-11 seasons in the past decade, Baylor managed to beat Kansas. That streak came to an end on Saturday in wild fashion. Baylor blew a 21-10 lead entering the fourth quarter as the offense imploded. Kansas blocked a potential 45-yard game-winning field goal to clinch the game as the Bears allowed more than 200 yards passing and rushing. While a loss to TCU seemed to spell the end of the Aranda era, losing in this fashion cements it. There's no path back for the Bears. Baylor has not fired a coach for on-field reasons since 2007, so it's unclear whether they'll make a midseason move. At this point, though, they're not doing anyone favors by dragging it out.  
Winner: ArizonaThe No. 25 Wildcats have flown under the radar since a tight loss against BYU in Week 2. But in a 39-3 win over Iowa State, the Wildcats are sneaking around the periphery of the Big 12 title race. Quarterback Noah Fifita is playing the best football of his career as he recorded his fifth straight game with at least 275 yards and two touchdowns. The defense is also finding its groove, holding the Cyclones' highly-touted rushing game to 1.7 yards per carry. Arizona deserves to be much higher than No. 25 in the AP Top 25. With a road trip to No. 8 Texas Tech next week, don't be surprised if everyone is talking about the 'Cats after next week. 
Loser: OregonThe Ducks have been such a disaster this season that it's almost flown under the radar. Oregon started the season as the preseason No. 2 team in the nation but fell to 4-3 after a stunning 21-10 loss to Illinois. Losses against Oklahoma State and UCLA are defensible, but losing to the Illini is where the season officially becomes a failure. The Ducks averaged only 6.0 yards per pass attempt as several receivers missed the game. But more frustrating, Illinois rushed for 225 yards against a rush defense heralded as one of the best in the nation. Oregon's collapse joins those at Penn State and LSU last season as some of the most frustrating in the College Football Playoff era, especially given the investment. Dan Lanning is in no danger of being fired at this point, but everyone else in the building is on the chopping block. 
Winner: South CarolinaAfter starting the season about as bad as they could, Shane Beamer's Gamecocks suddenly have life. South Carolina just picked up a second straight ranked win, and it could have three had it not fallen by one point to Kentucky. This time, it was a 27-24 upset against No. 11 Tennessee as time expired. South Carolina finally got a great running game from quarterback LaNorris Sellers, as he threw for 210 yards, rushed for 96 yards and scored three total touchdowns. The defense stepped up in big moments, including a late sack from defensive end Dylan Stewart. The Gamecocks only have one game remaining against an AP Top 25 opponent: No. 5 Georgia on Nov. 21. Could South Carolina clear eight wins? 
Loser: James MadisonThe Dukes were in a tremendous position to contend for the Group of Six's College Football Playoff spot. Unfortunately, historic Sun Belt power Appalachian State had something to say about it. James Madison lost 34-31 in overtime against the rival Mountaineers to fall to 7-1 and complicate its pathway to the Sun Belt title game. The Dukes earned only 92 yards rushing on 30 carries. But even if JMU retakes control of the Sun Belt race, their schedule won't give them much leeway compared to other Group of Six contenders. Winner: MinnesotaThe Golden Gophers might be the quietest 5-2 team in America, but Minnesota picked up a major victory over No. 15 Iowa 13-10 on a game-winning field goal. With the win, Minnesota now has wins over Iowa and Michigan in the same season for the first time since 2014. The next few weeks ahead are tough with No. 6 Indiana and No. 9 UCLA, but PJ Fleck has the program in a great spot.

title: 2026 World Series: Rays making too many mistakes to survive against Brewers - CBS Sports
description: Give the Brewers so much credit for their inevitability, but the Rays are handing them every opportunity
body:
Give the Brewers so much credit for their inevitability, but the Rays are handing them every opportunity
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:26 am ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        MILWAUKEE -- The 2026 Milwaukee Brewers are redefining relentless.They did it again. The Brewers fell behind early and came back to win. This time around, the Rays scored four runs in the first inning and the Brewers just chipped away until they finally (inevitably?) took the lead in the bottom of the seventh inning. They won, 5-4. They are masters of the comeback craft. It all started in Game 1 of the NLDS. The Padres took the early lead. The Brewers came back to win. It happened again in Game 2. They did it in all four games of the NLCS against the two-time defending champion Dodgers, including a four-run comeback in the Game 4 clincher. And now they've done it again. The Brewers are now 9-1 in the playoffs, and they've come from behind to win seven times. If that's not enough, some of the other numbers are downright staggering. The Brewers this year, regular season and playoffs combined, are now 41-37 when the other team scores first. That's a mind-boggling stat. The last team to finish a season with a winning record in such situations was the 2009 Yankees (via Sarah Langs). Or how about this one? The Brewers just became the fifth team in MLB playoff history to win multiple games after falling behind by at least four runs.
These Brewers are also just the third team to trail by four runs at home in the World Series and come back to win, along with the 2017 Astros and 2002 Angels."We're down to the end of the season here," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said after Game 2 on Saturday. "They're going to tap us on the shoulder here at some point and tell us no more. Guys just, they don't give up. They believe, and they don't give up. They just keep going."That said, I would be remiss to ignore the other component of World Series Game 2: the mistake-filled game the Rays just played. That absolutely cannot happen against a team as relentless as these Brewers. 
In the bottom of the first inning, Jonathan Aranda botched an attempt to catch a foul ball. William Contreras then singled and the Brewers scored twice that inning. In the bottom of the fourth, Aranda let a weak grounder go through his legs. The Brewers scored again, cutting the deficit to 4-3. In the top of the sixth, Liam Hicks was thrown out at home plate by Jackson Chourio after a single to left field. It makes sense to try and score the run with two outs, but Hicks was out by a country mile. It was the fourth out on the bases the Rays have made in the World Series. This was only the middle of Game 2. Sal Frelick homered to tie the game. He only hit four in the regular season. Give Frelick credit, of course, but that was another thing that just can't happen.Chandler Simpson couldn't hold on to a Christian Yelich pop fly in the sixth inning and the dropped ball put runners at first and third with two outs. The play was ruled a single and Tyler Wells got out of the inning, but it should have been caught.Not that it mattered much at the time, but the Brewers pulled off a double steal in the eighth, thanks in part to backup catcher Nick Fuentes bobbling the pitch. "Look, we didn't play our cleanest baseball game by any stretch," Rays manager Kevin Cash said after Game 2. "We pride ourselves on doing everything we can to support the pitchers and making plays behind them. Today was probably not our best day."The Milwaukee Brewers won 103 games in the regular season and posted the best run differential in baseball. They regularly come from behind to win. They create their own breaks so often. No team can expect to beat them in the playoffs by giving them gifts the way the Rays did in Game 2 of the World Series. It was unacceptable.Let's not get things twisted, though. The Brewers deserved to win this game and deserve to be up 2-0 in this series, just as they are. They are the better team and have played like it. 
Even if that send of Hicks to home was a bad decision, Chourio's throw was excellent, as was the work at home plate by Contreras. Also, the Rays scored four runs in the first inning and didn't score again. That's some outstanding mound work from the Brewers, especially their bullpen. JoJo Romero, Dustin May and DL Hall kept their team in the game before the Brewers tied it and then took the lead and dropped the proverbial hammer with late-inning beasts Abner Uribe and Aaron Ashby.The top of the first inning was a disaster, really, for the Brewers. Logan Henderson gave up four runs in a game for the first time in his (admittedly short) MLB career. Cooper Pratt started the game with a throwing error that opened the door. Hicks crushed a two-run home run to silence the crowd. But. And there's always a but with these Brewers, isn't there? Chourio led off the bottom of the first with a single and the comeback was on. The crowd seemed to sense it was inevitable from the get-go. The noise never wavered. They were electric all night, as if there was never a doubt. For the fans who have watched this team all season, there probably wasn't. 
From the press box, the second Sal Frelick hit his unlikely home run, the game seemed over. That blast merely tied the game, but we might as well have called the rest of the thing off. It was over the second that ball crossed over the center field wall. The Rays were cooked because the Brewers are just too good to be allowed to hang around. Even when the Rays got a leadoff double from Jonny DeLuca in the ninth, it never felt like a huge threat. They even got the runner to third base with Yandy Díaz coming to the plate. No matter. Brewers manager Pat Murphy stuck with Ashby and Ashby got the strikeout. The Brewers now only need to win two more games before they lose four to secure the first World Series title in franchise history. When they do clinch this thing, it won't be a surprise. It feels inevitable at this point, and if we start to doubt them, they'll remind us with another comeback. That's how relentless they are.
